claims.text: Structural and chemical stability across 473–1923 K is governed by formation of a stable, disordered atomic arrangement.
A stable, disordered atomic arrangement resists phase segregation.
A stable, disordered atomic arrangement maintains a uniform distribution of elements.
Nanoparticles retaining the disordered arrangement will remain structurally and chemically stable over 473–1923 K.
Lattice parameter and elemental composition will each deviate by less than 10% from the initial crystallized-solid-solution baseline.
Impurities, defects, or external factors may affect the stability of the disordered atomic arrangement.
The proposed test applies in situ TEM annealing and dual-beam irradiation with temperature ramps and holds at 473, 973, and 1923 K.
A deviation greater than 20% from baseline in either lattice parameter or elemental composition at any tested temperature would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires less than 10% deviation, whereas falsification requires more than 20% deviation. Outcomes from 10% through 20% would violate the prediction without meeting the stated falsification criterion, leaving the test indecisive.
